title: Stale route epoch stalls A/B split promotion and blocks rollback
creator: Maya Chen
description: During a staged A/B promotion for model-v2, promotion stalled and automatic rollback could not complete because a subset of routing proxies served a stale route epoch for the target path. This ticket captures the postmortem, investigation notes, mitigations applied, and action items to prevent recurrence.
impact_summary: ~12% of customer traffic was pinned to older variant during promotion window (approx. 16:18-16:52 UTC). Several low-latency SLA customers observed elevated 95p latency as requests were routed across mismatched model variants causing KV cache misses and tokenization mismatch errors. No secrets or data exfiltration detected.
timeline: 2026-03-10T16:12:00Z - Deployment started: rollout job kicked off to promote model-v2 via A/B split (weight 10%).
2026-03-10T16:18:00Z - Monitoring alert: discrepancy between desired route weights and observed traffic split. Some proxies reporting epoch 42 while control plane broadcast epoch 44.
2026-03-10T16:25:00Z - Attempts to force promotion via control-plane API returned success but probes showed mixed variant serve.
2026-03-10T16:32:00Z - Manual rollback initiated but rollback jobs reported stuck 'awaiting route-epoch-confirmation' on 7 out of 24 proxies.
2026-03-10T16:45:00Z - Mitigation: Defensive routing-rule override applied targeting region us-west-2 to force local proxies to accept epoch 44.
2026-03-10T16:52:00Z - Rollback completed after routing override; traffic returns to pre-rollout steady-state.
2026-03-10T17:05:00Z - Post-incident checks, brief customer notifications drafted.
investigation: Initial logs showed the control plane had successfully broadcast route epoch 44 but an intermediate cache invalidation path in the edge-config service failed to deliver the epoch bump to a subset of older proxies that had a stale long-lived connection. The stale proxies continued to honor epoch 42 causing them to ignore the rollback instruction which checks epoch alignment before accepting route changes. Root causes explored: (1) edge-config long-polling implementation had a regression in reconnect logic when behind certain TCP proxies, (2) route-epoch reconciliation had a silent failure path that suppressed error logs, (3) lack of an operator-visible metric for per-proxy epoch lag.
root_cause: A combination of an edge-config long-poll reconnect regression (deployed in runtime-1.26) and missing per-proxy epoch-lag instrumentation. Stale long-lived connections did not reconnect after the broadcast, leaving proxies stuck on the older epoch and rejecting rollback steps that required epoch confirmation.
mitigations_taken: Immediate: Applied routing-rule override to force acceptance of new epoch on affected region and triggered reconnect by toggling proxy healthcheck to break stale connection.
Near-term: Rolled back the runtime-1.26 edge-config patch to older stable image for the ephemeral fleet in us-west-2 to prevent repeat during rollouts.
Communication: Notified impacted customers and updated on Slack incident channel with status and remediation timeline.
action_items: 1) Add per-proxy epoch_lag metric and a Grafana dashboard to alert when any proxy lags by >1 epoch for >1m. Owner: Priya Patel. ETA: 2026-03-20.
2) Harden edge-config reconnect logic with unit and e2e tests that simulate TCP proxy interruption. Owner: Sandeep Rao. ETA: 2026-03-24.

3) Make route-epoch acceptance idempotent for rollbacks: if rollback attempts see older epoch, allow forced application with operator audit log and a safety throttle. Owner: Liam O'Connor. ETA: 2026-03-31.
4) Implement a 'force-accept' control-plane API handshake for emergency rollbacks with explicit operator confirmation and automated canary checks. Owner: Product/Platform. ETA: 2026-04-07.
5) Update runbook: add step to toggle proxy healthcheck/endpoints to force reconnect prior to manual rollback. Owner: Oncall SRE. ETA: 2026-03-15.
6) Post-deploy verification: require a per-region epoch-ack fence check in rollout pipeline; block promotion if any proxy fails ack within 30s. Owner: CI/CD team. ETA: 2026-03-28.
owners: Maya Chen (Release Engineer) - incident lead and postmortem author
Liam O'Connor (Platform Engineer) - rollback and code owner for control-plane
Priya Patel (SRE) - monitoring and alerts owner
notes: This incident highlighted a blind spot between control-plane broadcasts and edge delivery under network churn. The immediate workaround (force override + healthcheck toggle) is low friction but brittle; the long-term fix must focus on observability and deterministic rollout fencing. Avoid introducing VM-level reconnect regressions in mid-release windows; consider canarying edge-config patches only to short-lived fleets with aggressive reconnect testing.
